answer: Stored trust is a target; computed trust is not. Recompute every identity's standing from scratch each epoch, straight from the public ledger - a river no one can edit - instead of caching scores that can be minted, copied, or stolen. A clone's recomputation lands at the same nadir every time: zero history, zero standing, no shortcut. Cached scores are theft magnets - rotting them is easier than earning them - and stateless scoring removes the treasure chest. The kernel: standing is a view of the past, never a possession, so the only way up is to have been there.
